title: Cofinal restriction and the compact-support adjunction mate
statement:
Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ have characteristic $p$ and let $\ell\ne p$ be prime [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes, with no separatedness assumption on $Y$, and fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_f}Y$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For an inverse sequence $C_\bullet$ of finite commutative rings annihilated by powers of $\ell$, write $\mathscr S_C(W)$ for strict systems of $(C_n)_{W_{\mathrm{et}}}$-module sheaves, with $C_{n+1}$-linear transitions $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{C_{n+1}\to C_n}M_n$ and compatible componentwise morphisms, and use its ordinary unbounded derived category and evaluation $e_n$ [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension]. Set $F_C=Rp_{f,C,*}j_{!,C}$ and $F_{C_n}=Rp_{f,*,C_n}j_!$, where open extension and ordinary etale direct image act termwise before derivation [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. 
Let $r:\mathbf Z_{\ge1}\to\mathbf Z_{\ge1}$ be strictly increasing and unbounded, let $C_r=(C_{r(i)})_i$, and write $U_r^W:D(\mathscr S_C(W))\to D(\mathscr S_{C_r}(W))$ for restriction. Let $L_r^W\dashv U_r^W$ be derived left extension with $t(m)=\min\{i:r(i)\ge m\}$ and
$$e_mL_r^WN=C_m\otimes^L_{C_{r(t(m))}}N_{t(m)}$$
with the selected-level transitions and tensor associators of [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension]. The finite-ring projection maps of [lem-pur-etale-system-coefficient-projection] give a natural isomorphism
$$h_r:F_CL_r^X\xrightarrow{\sim}L_r^YF_{C_r},$$
whose level-$m$ component is the inverse of $q$ for $C_{r(t(m))}\to C_m$. It is a map of actual derived systems, with the specified transition maps.

Fix adjunctions $F_C\dashv G_C$ and $F_{C_r}\dashv G_{C_r}$ on the unbounded categories. There is a natural isomorphism $\rho_r:U_r^XG_C\cong G_{C_r}U_r^Y$ specified by the natural Hom bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(N,U_r^XG_CM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_r^XN,G_CM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_CL_r^XN,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_r^YF_{C_r}N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(N,G_{C_r}U_r^YM).$$
It preserves the counits after restriction, respects map action, and its comparisons for composite subsequences agree under the canonical composed-restriction and left-extension identifications. All maps are independent of resolutions on ordinary derived systems. In particular it applies to $C_m=O'/(v^m)$, $r(n)=en$ for $O'=\mathcal O_{E'}$ with $E'/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite and a uniformizer $v$: whenever $s\in O'$ satisfies $sO'=v^eO'$ with $e\ge1$, the quotient-ring identifications $O'/(v^{en})=O'/(s^n)$ carry the restricted construction, including its maps, to the construction using $O'/(s^n)$ and the same chosen compactification.

proof.text: Obtain the normalized geometric support realization, retaining invertibility and the coefficient-projection cocycle.
Apply the normalized geometric subsequence cocycle.

Prove the Hom action and counit equations by composite adjunction uniqueness. Identify each mate with conjugateEquiv. The mate of the inverse left-adjoint compositor is the restriction compositor. The whiskering and composition laws for conjugateEquiv transform the geometric cocycle into rho composition. These are proved generic private lemmas in the item module.

For $C_m=O'/(v^m)$ these are finite $\ell$-primary coefficient rings by the local-field coefficient-stage theorem with the identity field extension and uniformizer $v$. If $sO'=v^eO'$, taking $n$th ideal powers gives $s^nO'=v^{en}O'$. The canonical quotient identifications send the class of every $x\in O'$ to its class and commute with quotient maps because both routes send $x$ to the same class. Since $e\ge1$, $r(n)=en$ is strictly increasing and unbounded. Transport the systems, tensor functors and their specified units along these ring identifications. The map $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ and the quotient transitions are unchanged; the defining transpose for $q$, hence steps 2 and 4 and their counit equations, are unchanged as well. The compactification was fixed throughout. This proves the final specialization on objects and maps, including $e=1$.

Steps 4-6: composite adjunctions and the counit-uniqueness equation are type-checked, and the composite order (ρ_s U_r)(U_s ρ_r) is right.
